item.title: The Ontology Divide Is Not Model Size
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. Between December 2025 and November 2026, six papers closed in on one conclusion from three directions. The bottleneck in ontology construction moved from who can write an ontology to who can prove the written thing is right. Every number below goes back to a named section or table. Two minutes twenty-three, voiced in English, captions burned in and switchable in the player.

item.title: Retrieval as Navigation: DecisionRAG Asks a Tree Instead of Scoring a Corpus
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. The bottleneck in retrieval is not the size of the candidate pool. It is what you let the model see, and in which order. DecisionRAG replaces scoring with asking, and returns a 65.4 top-1 hit over 2.68M passages in 1.7 seconds. It also loses three cells, plainly. English voiceover, 3 minutes 12 seconds.

item.title: One Graph, Fifteen Spellings, a 28-Point Difference
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line. How a graph is spelled into a prompt is a measurable system parameter. It is worth 1.3 to 3.9 points on ontology extraction and 28.4 points on structural reasoning, and the three reasoning tiers of a single model family each prefer a different format, with the most accurate tier burning the fewest tokens.

item.title: The four-layer memory stack, and the dreaming loop beside it: reading Anthropic's memory research
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: memory is not a transcript you keep, it is cargo moved between four layers — the low ones are true and hard to use, the top one is easy and easy to get wrong. Dreaming is the worker that moves it while nobody is watching. Note on figures: the diagrams here are redrawn from the article’s own data and structure; its fifteen-odd figures and screenshots are at the source linked at the end.

item.title: Think Before You Act: How JevAct Gates LLM Agent Actions
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 This English page stays available at its own URL. The Chinese version is the one maintained first. English readers land here directly. To pin English after switching languages, use ?lang=en on this URL, e.g. this link. An agent’s action should pass through a gate that can check, compute, and send back before anything executes. JevAct splits that gate in two. code settles what tool records decide, a decision model answers only “what did the conversation actually say”, and a boolean rule combines them.
